title: Characterization of additive maps on the Boolean cube
statement: Let $f$ be a function from $ br^n$ with coordinates in the field of two elements to that field. Then $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y$ if and only if there is a subset $S$ of the coordinate indices $\\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that $f(x)=\sum_{i\in S}x_i$ for every $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from the $n$-dimensional coordinate space over the field of two elements to that field
